insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹5 Lakhs to ₹2 Crore (as per Schedule of Benefits)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured: The policy provides automatic restoration of sum insured... Sum Insured will be restored unlimited number of times and maximum up to 100% each time... The restoration will trigger immediately upon partial/ full utilization of the sum insured... The Restored Sum Insured can be used for all claims including for modern treatment, but for a subsequent hospitalization.
great.reference: Coverage, Clause 27 (Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured) (pages 5-6)
great.explanation: Sum Insured gets restored immediately after partial/full use, unlimited times, up to 100% each time. This can significantly increase available cover within the same policy year for subsequent hospitalizations.

great.name: Consumables
great.quote: Coverage for Non-medical Items (Consumables): If there is an admissible claim under inpatient / day care the policy, then Items as per List I will become payable
great.reference: Coverage, Clause 5 (page 3) + LIST I — ITEMS FOR WHICH COVERAGE IS AVAILABLE IN THE POLICY (pages 13-14)
great.explanation: Non-medical consumables are payable for an admissible inpatient/day care claim, as per the policy’s List I. This reduces out-of-pocket spend on items that many insurers exclude.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: Room, Boarding and Nursing charges: Up to 1% of Sum Insured per day (5 lacs)... Any Room (Except suite or above category) (10/15/20/25 lacs)... Any room (50/75/1 Crore/2 Crore)
good.reference: Schedule of Benefits, S.No. 1 Room, Boarding and Nursing charges (page 15)
good.explanation: Room rent is capped at 1% of Sum Insured per day at ₹5 lakh, while higher Sum Insured options allow any room (with some tiers excluding suite/above). This is flexible at higher covers but can be restrictive at ₹5 lakh.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Applicable for 1 year and 2 year policy term: ... excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage... Applicable for 3 year policy term: ... excluded until the expiry of 30 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months (1/2-year term) or 30 months (3-year term) of continuous coverage. This is within the common 2–4 year range in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Exclusions > Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code Excl 02) (page 8)
good.explanation: Listed specific diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard waiting period for such conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days, except if caused by an accident. This is the usual initial waiting period in most plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.reference: Coverage, Clause 8 (page 3) / Schedule of Benefits S.No.5 (page 15)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital.
good.reference: Coverage, Clause 9 (page 3) / Schedule of Benefits S.No.6 (page 15)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge are covered. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: Cumulative Bonus: ... calculated at 25% of sum insured for each claim free year and maximum up to 100%... In the event of a claim resulting in... Full utilization of Sum Insured and full utilization of cumulative bonus accrued, the cumulative bonus on renewal will be “nil”
good.explanation: Cumulative Bonus increases Sum Insured by 25% per claim-free year up to 100%. If a claim fully uses both base Sum Insured and the bonus, the bonus becomes nil at renewal.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Air Ambulance: Air ambulance expenses are payable... up to10% of sum insured per policy year
good.reference: Coverage, Clause 7 (page 3) / Schedule of Benefits S.No.4 (page 15)
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are covered up to 10% of Sum Insured per policy year. This can help in emergencies where rapid transfer is medically required.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Room, Boarding and Nursing charges: Up to 1% of Sum Insured per day... Note: Associated Medical expenses which vary based on the room occupied by the insured person will be considered in proportion to the room rent stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Schedule of Benefits S.No.1 (page 15) + Coverage Note under Clause 1 (page 3)
bad.explanation: If you choose a room above the eligible limit, associated medical expenses can be paid only in proportion to the allowed room rent. This can sharply increase your out-of-pocket costs even when the Sum Insured is high enough.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Assisted Reproduction Treatment (per policy year) 1,00,000/- (5 lacs) ... 2,00,000/- (10-25 lacs) ... 4,00,000/- (50 lacs and above)
bad.explanation: Assisted Reproduction Treatment has a per policy year cap (₹1,00,000 at ₹5 lakh SI; ₹2,00,000 at ₹10–25 lakh; ₹4,00,000 at ₹50 lakh+). Any expense beyond this limit is not payable even if your Sum Insured is higher.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured person whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.reference: Coverage, Clause 30 (Co-payment) (page 7) / Schedule of Benefits S.No.29 (page 16)
bad.explanation: A 10% co-pay applies on each and every claim if entry age is 61 years and above. This means you must pay 10% of admissible bills from your pocket on every claim.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
